# Linting instruction files for seeded vocabulary — facts

## Definitions

- [statement] Overused-word lists are the norm in public 'humanize' skills, e.g. a Tier 1 banned list of 18 words including delve, tapestry, pivotal, testament; such files embed the seeded tokens in the instruction file itself. (low confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://github.com/lguz/humanize-writing-skill · keywords: Linting instruction files for seeded vocabulary

## Problems, failure modes and limitations

- [statement] A mechanistic study of 40,000 samples reports that explicitly naming a forbidden word can raise its generation probability; priming failure accounts for 87.5% of negative-constraint violations and override failure for 12.5%. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08070 · keywords: Linting instruction files for seeded vocabulary · also: https://multigrid.ai/learn/negative-prompting
- [statement] The same study finds violation probability tracks the model's intrinsic 'semantic pressure' toward the token (p = sigmoid(-2.40 + 2.27*P0)), so the risk is highest for high-prior tics such as delve, which are exactly the ones people list. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08070 · keywords: Linting instruction files for seeded vocabulary

## Comparisons and alternatives

- [statement] Anthropic's prompting docs tell authors to say what to do instead of what not to do, and note that the formatting style of the prompt can influence response style, so instruction files should be written in the target voice. (high confidence) (verified as of 2026-09-23) — https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/build-with-claude/prompt-engineering/claude-prompting-best-practices · keywords: Linting instruction files for seeded vocabulary · also: https://multigrid.ai/learn/negative-prompting
- [statement] A workable lint design: scan instruction files for tokens on a tic list and classify each hit as ban-list entry, example text or incidental prose; flag examples and prose hits first, since they show the word as a model to copy rather than as a prohibition. This is inferred from the sources, not documented anywhere. (low confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08070 · keywords: Linting instruction files for seeded vocabulary

## Facts and statements

- [statement] Lexical overrepresentation (delve, intricate, underscore; 21 focal words in scientific abstracts) is not explained by architecture, algorithm or training data; RLHF is a suspect but evidence is mixed. The lint word list must therefore be empirical and per-model, not a fixed canon. (medium confidence) — https://arxiv.org/abs/2412.11385 · keywords: Linting instruction files for seeded vocabulary · also: https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.08070
